summary.title: Itanium C++ ABI
summary.one_liner: The Itanium C++ ABI specifies binary-level rules for C++ object layout, virtual tables, member pointers, calling conventions and exception handling, and is used as a base by many C++ platforms.
takeaways: How C++ objects, bases, and data members are laid out in memory, including tail padding and POD rules
How virtual tables are structured: primary and secondary vtables, address points, vcall offsets, and virtual base offsets
How data member pointers and member function pointers are represented, including the 32-bit ARM alternate form
The ABI is a generic spec layered on the platform C ABI; platforms may vary and should document their changes
summary.summary: This is the Itanium C++ ABI specification, a reference document that defines the object code interfaces between C++ program fragments and runtime libraries. It covers data layout (class and POD layout, member pointers), code emission and APIs, exception handling, and linkage and object files. The page is a formal spec organized into numbered chapters and written with precise, rule-based descriptions of allocation and vtable construction. The text shown here covers the introduction, data layout, and virtual table sections; the page itself does not describe the non-trivial temporary passing rule mentioned in the listing.
